findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
No paper towels were available at time of inspection.  Discussed with PIC, COS.  Ensure paper towels and soap are always available during hours of operation.

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
A mop was observed mop head down in the mop sink.  Discussed with PIC, COS.  Ensure mops are stored in a way to allow the mop to air dry to prevent mold and mildew growth.

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The hand sink is in need of re-caulking.  Discussed with PIC.  Ensure sink is caulked to create a smooth and easily cleanable surface.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
An employee was observed filling a bowl with water in the hand sink. The hand sink may not be used for any purposes other than hand washing. The manager was informed and education was provided to correct the violation. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Fruit flies were observed in the bag that contains old wiping cloths and aprons. The bag appeared to be the source of the fruit flies. The wiping cloths are supplied by CINTAS and containers are emptied twice per week. The bag was sealed to prevent fruit flies from leaving the bag and a lid was placed on the container. Fruit flies were not observed in any other part of the establishment. The manager stated CINTAS would be contacted to remove the bag, thus correcting the violation. 

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The walk in cooler fan was observed with an accumulation of dust and soil. Ensure the walk in cooler fan is cleaned at a frequency to maintain it clean. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: Observed butter exposed on shelf uncovered and at risk of contamination. Butter is going to be thrown away and replaced with fresh butter. Ensure that all products are covered during storage to prevent cross contamination.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.113: Observed the mops not being used stored in the mop sink and in the mop bucket that does not allow proper drainage and drying. Make sure mops are hung in a way that promotes drying and prevents bacterial growth. 
6-501.113: Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.
